subject: Listing copy & trial flow review — seller journey + edge cases
messages:
From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmedata.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft listing copy & trial scenarios for review

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. Attached is the updated listing draft and a quick diagram of how we expect the 14-day trial to route through our provisioning. Can you and the marketplace team double-check the usage examples and the "What you can build" bullets? We want to avoid any wording that could suggest managed services (it's a packaged inference offer) — AWS asked about that during intake.

Primary asks:
- Confirm the CTA wording aligns with private offer vs. public SKU
- Two short usage examples for "fraud detection" and "content summarization"
- An explicit trial-to-paid conversion flow for the marketplace page

Happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jennings
Head of Partnerships, Acme Data
sarah.jennings@acmedata.com
Attachment: listing_draft_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
Attachment: trial-flow-diagram.png (image/png)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmedata.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft listing copy & trial scenarios for review

Sarah —

Got it, thanks. Looping in Kim and Jonas for copy + entitlement checks.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- "What you can build" bullets are strong but the second example currently uses the phrase "fully managed" — suggest swapping to "packaged inference for" to avoid classification as managed service.
- Trial CTA: AWS prefers the CTA to emphasize "Start free trial" with a clear note on trial duration and required registration; avoid implying auto-conversion without consent.
- Pricing footnote: need to clarify per-token overage behavior during trial.

I'll leave the line edits to Kim; Jonas, can you confirm SKUs and private offer behavior for conversion paths?

—Aditya

Aditya Rao
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmedata.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft listing copy & trial scenarios for review

Thanks for the ping. I annotated the Word draft and made inline suggestions; high-level:

- Snippet changes: replace "fully managed" → "pre-packaged inference solution"; swap "deploy" language to "activate" for marketplace clarity.
- Usage examples: tightened to two concise bullets with expected token/sec and example pricing band — keeps buyer expectations realistic.
- Trial flow: added a short paragraph that explains entitlement checks, private offer assignment, and how the trial transitions to the reserved SKU — includes an opt-in box for billing.

Edge cases for product page copy:
- Customers in regulated sectors (HIPAA/PHI) should see a blurb about Private deployment options; propose a small inline link to the Private offering.
- Clearly call out data retention defaults during trial (14 days cached, KV cache persisted only if opted-in).

Action items:
- Sarah: can you confirm whether Acme wants the HIPAA blurb on the public page or only on the Private offering sub-page? If public, we may need legal signoff.
- Jonas: please validate the SKU mapping and whether conversion keeps trial metrics for billing reconciliation.

Kim

Kimberly Park
Go-to-Market Lead, Listings | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
Attachment: listing_draft_v2.docx (annotated)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmedata.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft listing copy & trial scenarios for review

All — quick confirmation after checking with ops.

- SKU behavior: trial uses a trial SKU that maps to a private offer on acceptance; conversion is opt-in and will not auto-charge. We can persist usage metrics for the first 7 days only (ops limit) — flagged in the copy update.
- AMI/AMI-like artifacts: need manifest file for marketplace listing; Sarah, please upload the manifest to the Drive link and confirm checksum.
- Legal: HIPAA blurb should live on the Private deployment page, not the public hero. We'll add a "See private options" link on the product page.

Next steps:
1) Sarah uploads manifest + confirms HIPAA scope (by EOD Tue)
2) Kim will deliver final copy for marketplace page by Thu
3) I will hand off SKU mapping doc to AWS marketplace ops and notify them of private offer ID once created

Jonas Weber
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
